contexts.statement: Clay Millennium Problem (P vs. NP): Pursue a genuinely publishable unconditional theorem on a concrete open frontier of P vs. NP: either (a) prove a new unconditional lower bound or separation in monotone/depth-bounded algebraic circuits, Polynomial Calculus / Frege proof complexity, or structured SAT / permanent-vs-determinant obstructions, or (b) prove a new sharp meta-complexity (MCSP / time-bounded Kolmogorov complexity) reduction or barrier theorem backed by an exact computer-verified certificate.

definitions.known_boundary: 强负面线索：多数仍处于搜索摘要或候选证据级，不能当作公认反例。 MIT News 报道，2002 年调查中有61名数学家和计算机科学家认为 $P$ 很可能不等于 $NP$，另有9人持相反看法。这是针对原问题的强负面信念证据，但所给摘要既未明确使用广泛共识措辞，也无多个独立强来源确立共识。 参考：[Explained: P vs. NP | MIT News | Massachusetts Institute of Technology](https://news.mit.edu/2009/explainer-pnp)；[My responses to GASARCH's P vs. NP poll](https://scottaaronson.blog/?p=690)；[I am conducting a NEW POLL on P vs NP](https://blog.computationalcomplexity.org/2011/06/i-am-conducing-new-poll-on-p-vs-np.html)

contexts.statement: Construct an explicit infinite family of rooted graphs G_n with n vertices and M_n=Theta(n) independent directed-edge variables such that both F_G+epsilon*T_G and F_G-epsilon*T_G require monotone arithmetic circuits of size at least 2^(a*n), for fixed a,b>0, all sufficiently large admissible n, and every epsilon in [2^(-b*n),1/2].

definitions.graph: Finite rooted loopless graph; each allowed arc (v,w) with v different from the root has its own variable x_(v,w); opposite orientations are distinct variables.
definitions.T_G: Sum of squarefree monomials of spanning arborescences directed toward the root, with coefficient one.
definitions.F_G: Product over nonroot vertices v of the sum of x_(v,w) over allowed outgoing neighbors w.
definitions.circuit_model: Binary addition and multiplication arithmetic circuits over independent directed-edge variables and nonnegative real constants; size is the number of arithmetic gates.
definitions.explicit_family: A deterministic polynomial-time procedure constructs the rooted graph on every admissible size in an unbounded sequence.
definitions.sparse: There are fixed positive constants c,C with c*n <= M_n <= C*n, counting every auxiliary vertex and independent arc variable.
definitions.distribution_requirement: One probability distribution on outgoing-neighbor assignments, independent of the vertex partition, must have exponentially small rectangle discrepancy for every partition of nonroot vertex groups into two parts each of size between one third and two thirds of the groups.
definitions.acceptance: The unconditional all-size theorem, exact certificates for computationally used identities and inequalities, independently checked sources, verified novelty and publishable significance, and Host-invoked independent Reviewer approval are required. A conditional lemma or finite check does not complete C3395.

contexts.statement: For the existing explicit R_n=2F_(G_n)-T_(G_n), establish an unrestricted monotone arithmetic circuit lower bound 2^Omega(M_n) for some explicitly fixed symmetric Boolean-cube approximation factor kappa_0>1. A smaller fixed factor does not prove the separate factor-4/3 claim.

definitions.model: Binary nonnegative-real arithmetic DAGs with sharing, repeated variables, and unrestricted degree; every Boolean input is quantified.
definitions.projection: P0=Project(Q) retains after Booleanization exactly one variable per group; D=Booleanize(Q)-P0.
definitions.sampler: The unchanged full correlated matching/order/block sampler Delta of the independently reviewed construction.
definitions.repair: Construct a consistent full-group circuit of size at most K*M_n^d*(s+1)^e, with constants independent of n,s,degree, whose Booleanization P is coefficientwise at most P0 and has original-Delta expected coefficient loss at most (2-kappa_0^2)/(8*kappa_0).
definitions.scope: Existing Boolean lift, exact full-group normalizer, sampler, A1-A11, I1-I12, and G1-G14 are reused; no generic efficient compatible-part extraction is assumed.

contexts.statement: For the existing R_n=2F_(G_n)-T_(G_n), prove the unrestricted fixed-factor Boolean-approximation lower bound through a coefficient-weighted rectangle representation on the full outgoing-choice domain, without changing the complete original Delta.

definitions.domain: Omega is the full product of allowed outgoing choices of the original g=N+2 source groups, not just the support of Delta.
definitions.model: BP1 allows arbitrary nonnegative real constants, shared binary arithmetic DAGs, powers and unrestricted degree; size s counts original arithmetic gates.
definitions.rectangle: A times B across a balanced partition S of the original source groups, with g/3<=|S|<=2g/3; every nonnegative rectangle weight counts.
definitions.retention: Pointwise 0<=g<=h_Q is required on all of Omega; expected loss is under the unchanged complete Delta.
definitions.source_boundary: Reviewed exact epsilon-sensitive bounds and tropical monomial-overlap approximation do not supply Boolean-value consistency repair.

contexts.statement: Test coefficient-sensitive compatible-core extraction on explicitly declared product domains and laws; these diagnostics do not replace the original BP1 target or Delta.

definitions.literal_core: Nonnegative coefficient subfamilies of Boolean-aggregated factors from an actual compulsory cut, with every cross-pair compatible. Arbitrary positive rescaling and valid repartitioning of each core are allowed, but factoring a pooled sum of different cores is a separate operation.
definitions.calibration_domain: g=kt binary source groups partitioned into t blocks of size k divisible by three, with a balanced original side meeting each block in k/3 groups.
definitions.calibration_law: Uniform on the 2^t full assignments constant within each block; this law is mu and is not the production Delta.
definitions.calibration_target: F, with one-hot output identically one; this is not R_n and gives no small circuit for R_n.

external_assumptions.statement: For a 0-1 coefficient set-multilinear polynomial f and a single distribution Delta on its complete monomial domain, let gamma be the maximum rectangle discrepancy over all nearly balanced partitions of variable groups. claims.natural_statement: The original walk-conditioning approach requires a uniform lower bound on survival of a linear-length injective expander walk whose exponential loss is smaller than the unconditioned honored-gadget failure exponent. This required estimate has not been proved in this campaign.

Let H_N be a connected simple graph of maximum degree at most a fixed D>=2 such that every vertex cut with both sides of size at least N/4 has at least h*N crossing edges, for fixed h>0. Put kappa=h/(32*D^3) and take a fixed integer L>=8/kappa. On H_N^(14L) augmented by a root and two hubs, there is a partition-independent distribution on outgoing-neighbor assignments with rectangle discrepancy at most 3*exp(-kappa*N/(2*L^5)) for every nearly balanced partition of the N+2 nonroot vertices, for all sufficiently large N. The augmented graph has N+3 vertices and Theta(N) directed-arc variables.

For any finite nonempty unequal variable-group domains and any 0-1 coefficient set-multilinear polynomial f, if one distribution on the full product domain has rectangle discrepancy at most gamma for every nearly balanced group partition, then for gamma<=1/4 and 8*gamma<=epsilon<=1/2 both F+epsilon*f and F-epsilon*f require monotone arithmetic circuits of size at least epsilon/(6*gamma). Here F is the product of the sums in each group and the number of groups exceeds two.

There is a deterministic polynomial-time constructible infinite family of connected simple graphs H_N of bounded maximum degree D and a fixed h>0 such that every cut with both sides of size at least N/4 has at least h*N crossing edges.

external_assumptions.statement: Construction 8.1 on (Z/mZ)^2 uses T1=[[1,2],[0,1]], T2=[[1,0],[2,1]], translations e1,e2, and the four inverse transformations, giving an undirected 8-regular multigraph, possibly with loops. claims.natural_statement: Let R=2F-T have coefficients one and two on the full-group monomials, and let Q have nonnegative coefficients and satisfy R/kappa<=Q<=kappa*R on the entire Boolean cube. Replace each positive exponent in Q by one to get BQ, and retain only monomials using one variable from every group to get P0. Every monomial of Q meets every group. P0 approximates R coefficientwise with the same factor kappa; BQ approximates R on [0,1]^M; and on every Boolean point 0<=BQ-P0<=(kappa-1/kappa)*R. For kappa=4/3 and common arborescence discrepancy gamma<1/17, any monotone formal circuit computing P0 has size at least (1-17*gamma)/(32*gamma). No circuit-size upper bound for computing BQ or P0 from Q is asserted.

Unproved sufficient condition, not an available lemma: there are fixed constants d,e such that for every monotone size-s circuit Q satisfying the full Boolean-cube factor-4/3 inequalities for R_n=2F_(G_n)-T_(G_n), its Booleanized full-group component P0 has a monotone formal circuit of size at most M_n^d*(s+1)^e. Together with C3395-BOOLEAN-LIFT and the reviewed exponential discrepancy bound this would imply C3395-BOOLEAN-APPROX. Existence of the polynomial P0 alone does not establish this circuit bound.

For every integer g>=1 and d>=3, put A=product_{i=2}^g(u_i+v_i), P=(x+2y)*A and Q=(x^d+2*y^d+x*y)*A, with groups {x,y},{u_i,v_i}. On the entire Boolean cube P<=Q<=(4/3)*P. P is full-group with coefficient levels one and two. Nevertheless Q has no degree-g component, its least homogeneous component is x*y*A of degree g+1, and its Booleanization contains the forbidden same-group monomial x*y*A. Thus Boolean factor-4/3 approximation does not justify the continuous-cube least-component argument or the exact-counting consistency hypothesis. This easy family is not the sparse arborescence family and does not refute C3395-BOOLEAN-APPROX.

Let a nonnegative binary arithmetic circuit with s gates and arbitrary sharing have its variables in g nonempty groups X_i, and suppose every output monomial meets every group. Prune zero and unused gates. Let S_v be the groups in gate v, and T_v the union of groups in all productive one-occurrence output contexts of v. Equivalently T_root is empty, additions propagate the parent context, and products also propagate the sibling scope, taking unions over all uses. Put I_v=S_v intersect T_v and B=max_v product_{i in I_v}|X_i|. Its Booleanized full-group component has a formal monotone circuit of size at most 2*(g+2)*(s+1)*B^3. The construction memoizes one message per gate and assignment to I_v; it handles repeated variables, same-group conflicts, and shared gates without a formal-degree bound. The exponential dependence on the interface B is not a proof of B2.

For every unrestricted factor-4/3 Boolean approximator Q to the reviewed R_n, let s be its size, g its number of outgoing groups, and B the context-interface product from C3395-BOOLEAN-INTERFACE. If the common discrepancy gamma is at most 1/34, then (s+1)*B^3 >= 1/(128*(g+2)*gamma). Thus log2(s+1)+3*log2(B) >= log2(1/gamma)-log2(128*(g+2)). This forces exponential size when log2(B)=o(M_n), but large interfaces remain an unresolved case; the unrestricted size lower bound does not follow.

Given the reviewed exponential discrepancy bound and Boolean coefficient lift, the proposed existence bound B2 is equivalent to the target Boolean-approximation lower bound B up to fixed exponent constants. Every full-group polynomial on M variables has a monotone circuit of at most 2^M-1 gates by listing monomials, since product_i |X_i| <= 2^(M-g) and g+1<=2^g. Therefore an assumed lower bound s>=2^(c*M) on the original approximator already implies B2 with d=0 and e>=1/c. Conversely B2 combined with the reviewed lower bound for P0 implies B. This equivalence is a diagnostic of the remaining proof gap, not evidence that either assertion is true.

For every g>=1 and r>=2, let P=(x+2y)*product_{i=2}^g(u_i+v_i), H=P(1)=3*2^(g-1), and Q=P+P^r/(3*H^(r-1)). On the full Boolean cube P<=Q<=(4/3)*P. Repeated squaring computes Q with O(g+log r) monotone gates and can reuse subcircuits whose contexts overlap all g groups, giving interface product 2^g. Hence Boolean approximation by itself cannot imply a polynomial bound on the original circuit syntax interface or on repeated degrees. This easy target is not the arborescence family and does not refute B or B2.

Let a nonnegative binary arithmetic circuit with s gates and arbitrary sharing have its variables in g nonempty groups X_i, and suppose its output is nonzero and every output monomial meets every group. Prune zero and unused gates. Let S_v be the groups in gate v, and T_v the union of groups in all productive one-occurrence output contexts of v. Equivalently T_root is empty, additions propagate the parent context, and products also propagate the sibling scope, taking unions over all uses. Put I_v=S_v intersect T_v and B=max_v product_{i in I_v}|X_i|. Its Booleanized full-group component has a formal monotone circuit of size at most 2*(g+2)*(s+1)*B^3. The construction memoizes one message per gate and assignment to I_v; it handles repeated variables, same-group conflicts, and shared gates without a formal-degree bound. The exponential dependence on the interface B is not a proof of B2.

Let R=2F-T have coefficients in {1,2} on full-group monomials, and let Q<=kappa*R on the Boolean cube. Let U,V have nonnegative coefficients, satisfy UV<=Q on that cube, and have every monomial meeting each group in I. Fix one variable in every group outside I and nonempty variable subsets Y_i inside I. For each transversal z in Z=product_i Y_i let t_z=U(z)V(z), with the fixed outside assignment understood, and let K=|Z|. Then sum_z sqrt(t_z)<=sqrt(kappa*R(Y))<=sqrt(2*kappa*K). In particular, sum_z t_z/K<=2*kappa/sqrt(K). For an arbitrary conditional probability mu on Z the derived bound is E_mu[t]<=min(2*kappa,2*kappa*sqrt(K)*max_z mu(z)); it need not decay on a correlated sampler. This is a union coefficient-mass estimate, not an unrestricted circuit lower bound.

For every fixed q-block embedding E in the actual G_n sampler, q>=1, there is an O(g)-gate nonnegative polynomial H_E with H_E<=F_G on the entire Boolean cube. Its full-group Boolean projection is the zero-one polynomial of the diagonal embedded assignments with IP_q(x,y)=0. Thus Q_E=R_n+H_E/3 is a valid unrestricted factor-4/3 Boolean approximator (no small-size claim for Q_E). H_E/3 factors as U_E*V_E where U_E uses a balanced set S of groups, V_E uses the complement and overlaps U_E on all 2q a-vertex groups. All q gadgets are honored for S, yet E_{Delta_E}[(2f-1)*coefficient(P(U_E V_E))]=-(1+2^(-q))/6, while the conditional rectangle discrepancy for S is at most 2^(-q/2). Therefore Boolean domination, balanced factor scope, and conditional discrepancy do not imply an exponentially small per-product coefficient charge. The construction depends on E and does not refute a global estimate under the original embedding mixture Delta, B2, or the target lower bound.

Open direct sufficient condition, not established: there exist fixed positive constants K,d,e,delta such that every size-s unrestricted factor-4/3 Boolean approximator Q to R_n satisfies Lambda_Delta(P Q)>=-K*M_n^d*(s+1)^e*gamma^delta under the original joint embedding-mixture sampler. Together with the reviewed upper bound Lambda_Delta(P Q)<=-(1-17*gamma)/12 and gamma=2^(-Omega(M_n)), this would prove the unrestricted target. A valid proof must couple the same circuit across embeddings or otherwise use its size; the per-fixed-embedding product estimate is false.

For the actual common sampler Delta with q=floor(N/L) blocks, the fixed-embedding witness H_E from C3395-BOOLEAN-CONDITIONAL-MASS-OBSTRUCTION satisfies abs(Lambda_Delta(P(H_E/3))) <= (1/3)*binom(L,4)^(-q). Every one-hot assignment in its projection support has exactly the fixed embedding active base-vertex set S_E. Conditional on any sampled matching/order, that set is selected with probability either zero or binom(L,4)^(-q), since each full block independently chooses a uniform four-subset. Coefficients of P H_E are zero or one, yielding the bound after averaging. Thus the conditional obstruction has exponentially small global mass when its embedding is fixed in advance. This does not bound arbitrary circuit gates that may combine many embeddings with shared subcircuits.

Let g>=4 and let a nonzero size-s binary monotone arithmetic DAG have every output monomial meeting all g groups. For each productive gate v let G_v be the groups met by every monomial at v. There is an exact formal identity Q=sum_(j=1)^k A_j*V_j with k<=s, where each A_j is an original gate polynomial with g/3<=|G_(A_j)|<=2g/3, and every monomial of V_j meets the complement of G_(A_j). All coefficients are nonnegative, so each product is coefficientwise dominated by Q. Setting all such gates to zero annihilates the output. Cut them in reverse topological order and use positive divided-difference recurrences, not ordinary derivatives, to obtain the identity in one shared DAG with at most 4*s^2+3*s arithmetic gates, independent of formal degree, parse-tree count, interface size, and number of represented embeddings. Factors may overlap arbitrarily and have optional groups outside their compulsory sets; this is not a set-multilinear projection or a proof of B2.

For any size-s unrestricted factor-4/3 Boolean approximator Q of the actual R_n, with gamma<=1/34 and g>=4, the compulsory-cut decomposition contains a product A*V with a balanced exact compulsory group set for A and complementary compulsory groups in V such that A*V<=Q coefficientwise and Lambda_Delta(P(A*V))<=-1/(24*s) under the original joint sampler. The factors are represented by a shared DAG of size at most 4*s^2+3*s. This follows by linearity from the reviewed bound Lambda_Delta(P Q)<=-(1-17*gamma)/12 and at most s product terms; it does not count embeddings. It is an exact reduction to a global overlapping-product witness, not a lower bound excluding that witness.

Open stronger sufficient condition, not asserted true: for fixed positive K,d,delta, any nonnegative polynomials A,V with exact compulsory set S for A satisfying g/3<=|S|<=2g/3, with every V-monomial meeting the complement, and with A*V<=4*R_n/3 on the full Boolean cube, satisfy Lambda_Delta(P(A*V))>=-K*M_n^d*gamma^delta under the original joint embedding-mixture sampler. Factors may have arbitrary optional scopes and overlap; no conditional-embedding distribution may replace Delta. Combining this with the exact compulsory-cut decomposition would give U11 with e=1 and an exponential unrestricted lower bound. If the size-free condition fails, a size-sensitive bound for the extracted original-gate/context pairs remains a separate possible route.

Use the actual G_n sampler with D=8,h=1/64,kappa=2^(-20),L=2^23,N>=2^142 and g=N+2. Fix a balanced group partition S,barS. Let A,V be nonzero nonnegative polynomials such that every monomial of A uses exactly the group set S union T and every monomial of V exactly barS union U, where T is contained in barS and U in S; positive exponents and within-group conflicts are allowed. If A*V<=C*F_G on the whole Boolean cube, then abs(Lambda_Delta(P(A*V)))<=3*C*exp(-N/2^138), independent of factor size and overlap count. For overlap I=T union U below eta*N, eta=2^(-11), retained cut edges avoiding I give the signed bound. For larger I, uniform three-candidate switching of the b_(i,1) slot when x_i=0 yields E_Delta[A*V]<=C*exp(-eta^2*N/(1152*L)), hence the same bound. The switch is an exact augmentation of the original joint law, not a fixed-embedding replacement. This settles fixed group supports only, not optional-support mixtures in C8.

For a valid approximator Q, split each factor in its compulsory-cut decomposition by the exact set of groups appearing in a monomial. For each resulting product W define d(W)=max_{Boolean x:F_G(x)>0} W(x)/F_G(x), and let B_scope be the sum of these d(W) over all cut products and support components. The global fixed-support lemma and exact linearity give abs(Lambda_Delta(P Q))<=3*exp(-N/2^138)*B_scope, so gamma<=1/34 implies B_scope>=exp(N/2^138)/72. This is a domination-budget bound, not a bound on gate count: neither the number of support components nor their summed separate maxima is bounded here by a polynomial in circuit size.

For every k>=1, use groups {u_i0,u_i1} and {z_i,w_i}, let F=product_i(u_i0+u_i1)*(z_i+w_i), A=product_i(u_i0+u_i1*z_i), and V=product_i(z_i+w_i). Then A*V<=F on the full Boolean cube, G(A) is the balanced set of u-groups, and A*V has a (5*k-1)-gate monotone DAG. A has exactly 2^k group-support components A_T, and each product A_T*V has domination norm max_{Boolean x:F(x)>0} A_T(x)*V(x)/F(x)=1. Thus the sum of the separate component domination norms is 2^k, despite total product norm 1 and linear gate count. Q=F+A*V/3 is a valid factor-4/3 Boolean approximator of the easy full-group target F. This refutes a generic polynomial bound on the component-max budget for one product, not C8, U11, B2, or the actual arborescence lower bound.

Candidate extension of the unused-slot large-overlap step: on a product of k uniform one-active-candidate kernels, a nonnegative product A*V<=C*F with A compulsory on all candidate groups, V compulsory on balanced complementary padding groups, and every V monomial optional on at least one third of the candidate groups in every block has unsigned expected mass at most K*C*exp(-c*k), for absolute K,c>0 independent of k and the factors. Supports may vary between V monomials. This is a proposed local inference for a global proof, not a statement replacing the original sampler in C8.

For the original G_n sampler with N>=2^142 and theta=2^(-150), let G(A)=S be balanced, barS be contained in G(V), and A*V<=C*F_G on the Boolean cube. Decompose A,V by exact optional group supports T subset barS and U subset S, and let W_low=sum_(|T|+|U|<=theta*N) A_T*V_U. Then abs(Lambda_Delta(P W_low))<=3*C*exp(-N/2^139). The number of these pairs is at most sum_(i<=floor(theta*N)) binom(N+2,i)<=exp(N/2^139), so the reviewed fixed-support estimate applies without a polynomial separate-maxima budget. Consequently a size-s approximator in B with s<=exp(N/2^139)/384 has a fixed compulsory-cut product whose complementary coupled W_high has signed mass at most -1/(48*s). This controls the entire small-overlap band, not the remaining high-overlap signed mass or circuit size.

For every m>=2, 1<=t<=floor(m/2), k>=1, use k blocks of m two-variable groups {r_li,z_li}, plus km singleton padding groups with product Z. Set D_l=sum_i z_li*product_(j!=i) r_lj, B_l=e_t(r_l1,...,r_lm)/binom(m-1,t), A=product_l D_l, V=Z*product_l B_l, and F=Z*product_(l,i)(r_li+z_li). Then A*V<=F on the entire Boolean cube, G(A) and G(V) are complementary balanced sets, and every V monomial has t optional groups per candidate block. Under the product law choosing exactly one active z and all other r in each block, with padding one, A*V=F=1 pointwise and P(A*V)=Z*A. The family has O(k*m*t) monotone gates. Each of binom(m,t)^k support components has norm binom(m-1,t)^(-k) and mass binom(m,t)^(-k). Thus optional large overlap does not give a uniform unsigned exponential contraction for this exact one-active-candidate kernel, even at linear size with m=6,t=3. This refutes the proposed local unsigned optional-switch inference, not C8 or U11 under the full original sampler; fixing the local candidate blocks and targets after an embedding does not produce factors fixed before Delta.

Open residual sufficient condition: with theta=2^(-150), gamma=2^(-(N+3)/2^138), and the original full G_n sampler, there exist fixed K,d,delta>0 such that every nonnegative pair with balanced G(A)=S, barS contained in G(V), and A*V<=4*R_n/3 on the full Boolean cube has Lambda_Delta(P W_high)>=-K*M_n^d*gamma^delta, where W_high is the coupled sum of optional-support products A_T*V_U with |T|+|U|>theta*N. No conditioning on a support or embedding and no polynomial budget for separate component maxima is allowed. Together with the small-overlap bound this would imply C8; a size-sensitive substitute for actual extracted pairs could instead imply U11. No such high-overlap signed estimate is established by the local unsigned counterexample.

For the original sampler, balanced S=G(A), complement(S) contained in G(V), and A*V<=C*F_G on the Boolean cube, delete from A every monomial using a nonroot arc sourced outside S, and analogously from V outside complement(S), obtaining A_r,V_r. Then abs(Lambda_Delta(P(A_r*V_r)))<=3*C*exp(-N/2^136). The original O1 high-support sub-sum W_high^r formed from these filtered factors satisfies abs(Lambda_Delta(P W_high^r))<=6*C*exp(-N/2^139). Consequently a size-s approximator with s<=exp(N/2^139)/1536 has an actual fixed cut pair whose nonnegative remainder W_high^act=W_high-W_high^r satisfies Lambda_Delta(P W_high^act)<=-1/(96*s). This isolates optional nonroot dependence without choosing factors after sampling; it does not bound that dependence by circuit size.

Unproved size-sensitive sufficient condition for the live Boolean approximation target: there are K,c>0 and d,e>=0, independent of n,s and formal degree, such that every original gate/context pair extracted by C2 from a size-s unrestricted factor-4/3 Boolean approximator satisfies Lambda_Delta(P W_high^act)>=-K*M_n^d*(s+1)^e*exp(-c*N). Here W_high^act is the original O1 coupled high-support sum minus its root-only optional sub-sum, all factors fixed before the original matching/order/embedding/bit sampler. Together with C3395-BOOLEAN-ROOT-OPTIONAL-MASS and the complementary size range, this would prove size 2^Omega(M_n). No estimate of this strength is established.

For each fixed original-sampler embedding E, the O(g)-gate construction S1-S2 in signed-charge.tex has exact balanced complementary compulsory sets and H_E^*=A_E*V_E<=F_G on the full Boolean cube. Every surviving optional nonroot occurrence has a selected incoming arc in its own A_E monomial. Its coupled heavy part is entirely active and has conditional signed mass -Pr[Bin(q,1/2)>floor(theta*N/2)]/2<=-1/4. The coefficient-weighted optional-nonroot incidence I_0 at unused b slots on x_i=0 is identically zero under every embedding in the original full sampler. Nonetheless its full-sampler heavy signed mass is strictly negative, with magnitude at most binom(L,4)^(-q). It refutes unused-slot-only observability or a charge with no independent remainder, not the size-sensitive active charge or the requested unrestricted lower bound. The same product divided by three can occur in an actual compulsory cut of R_n+H_E^*/3, but no small size is asserted for that approximator.

Diagnostic-only shortcut, tested here rather than assumed: for every fixed balanced-compulsory factor pair dominated by F_G, the negative original-sampler mass of its coupled active heavy-support part is at most B*I_0 for some finite nonnegative B, where I_0 is the coefficient-weighted optional nonroot incidence at unused b slots with x_i=0 as defined in S7. There is no separate embedding-mixture remainder in this assertion. This is weaker in purpose, but not a replacement for, the live size-sensitive exponential estimate.

Open circuit-wide sufficient condition for the unchanged Boolean target: there are fixed K,c,e>0 and d>=0 such that every size-s unrestricted monotone circuit satisfying (3/4)R_n<=Q<=(4/3)R_n on the entire Boolean cube obeys Lambda_Delta(P Q)>=-1/48-K*M_n^d*(s+1)^e*exp(-c*N), with the original full sampler and constants independent of formal degree. Combined with the reviewed upper bound -1/24 this implies size 2^Omega(M_n). The surplus bound D<=7R_n/12 and exact gate accounting alone do not prove this estimate.

Propositions A1-A11 of research/boolean-circuit-charge/circuit-charge.tex: Booleanized surplus has an exact positive sum over actual product gates using ordered mixed original/compatible contexts, valid for arbitrary sharing, repeated variables, and nonnegative real constants; its common-input normalized total is at most 7/6 for an approximator. In each original compulsory-cut pair, the coupled sum having at most theta*N optional nonroot source groups, theta=2^(-150), has absolute original-sampler signed mass at most 3*C*exp(-N/2^139), despite arbitrary optional root groups. Thus s<=exp(N/2^139)/384 forces a fixed pair whose complementary sum, with more than theta*N optional nonroot source groups, has signed mass at most -1/(48*s). This strengthens the reviewed active witness but does not bound it by circuit size. Compatible filtering is semantic; no efficient ordinary circuit implementation or signed multi-hot transport is asserted.

Unproved T1 in research/boolean-circuit-charge/circuit-charge.tex: for every size-s unrestricted full-Boolean-cube factor-4/3 approximator Q, let H_> be the sum over its unchanged compulsory-cut pairs of exactly those monomial pairs with more than 2^(-150)*N optional nonroot source groups, keeping all coefficients. There exist fixed K,c,e>0,d>=0 and one probability measure mu_Q on multi-hot Boolean inputs with F_G>0 such that -Lambda_Delta(P H_>) <= (1/56)*integral (BQ-PQ)/F_G dmu_Q + K*M_n^d*(s+1)^e*exp(-c*N), under the original full sampler. No separate measure or maximum may be summed per support, monomial, or gate. Exact first-conflict accounting and the count of active source groups do not supply this signed transport, especially when selected incoming arcs must change with a switched source.

Construction I1-I12 in research/boolean-circuit-charge/incoming-resampling.tex: fix the original matching/order and two a vertices per block, but allow all ordered pairs of m candidate b sources, 3<=m<=L/4. The shared O(g+q*m^2)-gate pair has exact balanced complementary compulsory sets and H=A*V<=F_G on the entire Boolean cube. The conditional law resamples both candidate sources and their selected incoming arcs, with original uniform bits. Its high optional-nonroot contribution has signed mass -Pr[Bin(q,1/2)>floor(theta*N/2)]/2<=-1/4, while normalized Boolean surplus is at most one under every common multi-hot measure. Hence a conditional 1/56 surplus charge, even with a polynomial-in-factor-size exponentially decaying remainder for fixed m, is false. Under the original full sampler the signed magnitude is strictly positive but at most (4/L)^(2*q), because every supported assignment activates a fixed set of 2*q compulsory a vertices. The same factor can occur in an actual cut of R_n+H/3, without any small-size claim for that approximator. This excludes only the conditional incoming-source transport, not T1 or the unrestricted theorem.

For the unchanged full sampler Delta, put L=2^23, q=floor(N/L)>=2, and m=q-1. Let two complete independent draws form their Boolean union U, and choose a uniform one-hot corner of U. Its law Gamma satisfies Gamma(supp Delta) <= (3/4)^(m/2)+(8/sqrt(L))^m <= 2*exp(-m/8). For every full-group set-multilinear polynomial P, normalized evaluation P(U)/F_G(U) is exactly its uniform-corner coefficient average. A normalized nonnegative reweighting of the complete pair with density at most B can dominate c0*Delta through those corners only if B >= (c0/2)*exp(m/8). This is an all-size obstruction to coefficient-independent polynomial-in-N positive normalization, not a refutation of circuit-dependent polynomial-in-s transport or a lower bound for approximators. A4 and A5 retain their exact single-measure budget, but no signed heavy-mass comparison is proved.

Both compulsory and optional active vertices and both matching/order histories vary; no small-approximator hypothesis is imposed. This would only provide a generic positive normalization step, not the signed defect charge itself.

claims.natural_statement: Proposed diagnostic, to be tested rather than assumed: a vanishing full-cube relative output defect alone permits retaining all but o(1) original-Delta coefficient mass by replacing each defective product by a single consistent product of coefficientwise subpolynomials of its original children, without splitting or algebraic replacement. No size-sensitive remainder or special source of retention is included.

Conditional reduction N1-N4: for any fixed 1<kappa<sqrt(2), a consistent full-group P<=P0 with original-Delta expected coefficient loss at most (2-kappa^2)/(8*kappa), and gamma<=(2-kappa^2)/(2*(kappa^2+2)), has Lambda_Delta(P)<=-(2-kappa^2)/(8*kappa) and formal monotone size at least (2-kappa^2)/(16*kappa^2*gamma). The reviewed exact normalizer turns a polynomial-size repair into the desired unrestricted exponential lower bound. This proves an implication, not existence of a repair or any achieved factor.

All-size N5-N12 on the infinite admissible subsequence L|N: let r=4N/L, t=N-r, U be the full-group polynomial selecting exactly r base nonroot targets, and V=(sum base root variables)/t. For A=F_G or A=R_n-U, Q=A+UV projects to P_*=A+U and satisfies P_*<=Q<=(1+eta_N)P_* on the entire Boolean cube, with eta_N=sqrt(2*(b0+1)*r)/t=O(N^(-1/2)) and one defective product. Any single consistent U_prime*V_prime with coefficientwise U_prime<=U and V_prime<=V retains at most b_N=N/(t*(r+1))*(r/(r+1))^r=O(1/N) expected coefficient mass under the original full Delta, versus original mass one. h such products retain at most h*b_N. The easy-target circuit is polynomial-size; the actual-R_n version is not asserted small. This refutes size-free deletion-only stability, not polynomial-size algebraic repair or the target lower bound.

Exact replacement N13-N14: for a formal full-group W with a size-s_W monotone circuit, Project(W*(a0+sum_x a_x*x))=a0*W+sum_x a_x*x*dW/dx has a shared-DAG monotone circuit of size at most 4*s_W+M+2. If S_Y sums N distinguished variables at most one per group and p is a nonnegative univariate size-s_p circuit of arbitrary degree, Project(W*p(S_Y))=sum_{j=0}^N p(j)*W_j has size at most 2*(N+1)^2*s_W+(N+1)*(s_p+1)+N. W_j retains monomials with exactly j distinguished variables. Both preserve all projected coefficients and repair the N5-N12 family exactly. They assume an available consistent full-group factor and do not give a recursion for general unrestricted gates.

Open Reviewer action: every size-s unrestricted symmetric factor-6/5 Boolean approximator Q of the existing R_n admits a consistent full-group nonnegative arithmetic circuit of size at most K*M_n^d*(s+1)^e for fixed K,d,e>0, independently of formal degree, whose Booleanization P is coefficientwise <=P0=Project(Q) and has original-Delta expected coefficient loss <=7/120. No efficient semantic compatible-part extraction is assumed. The claim is not the stronger factor-4/3 assertion.

Candidate intermediate inference, not assumed: for a full-group product UV having uniformly vanishing relative Boolean defect in an approximator with one defective gate, polynomially many explicitly enumerated consistent products U_i*V_i, with coefficientwise U_i<=U and V_i<=V and no rescaling beyond those bounds, retain at least 113/120 of a unit original-Delta contribution. Polynomial counts are measured in M and the small product representation, not a possibly large surrounding actual-target circuit. This restricted inference is distinct from general algebraic repair and from a circuit that implicitly shares exponentially many summands.

P1-P10: with the reviewed slice U, r=4N/L, t=N-r, and V_d=(sum root variables/t)^d, Project(U*V_d)=U and every Delta sample has coefficient one. Q_d=A+U*V_d, for A=F_G or R_n-U, has one productive defective gate and relative full-Boolean-cube defect at most d*(N/t)^(d-1)*sqrt(2*(b0+1)*r)/t. Every consistent coefficientwise subproduct U_prime<=U, V_prime<=V_d retains at most beta=(N/t)^d*(d/(r+d))^d*(r/(r+d))^r original-Delta mass. On N=2^(24+2*d), d=2^j, j>=30, the approximation factor is <=6/5 while beta<=2^(-d^2). Retaining 113/120 of the contribution requires at least (113/120)*2^(d^2) explicitly enumerated unscaled subproducts. This is not a shared-DAG gate lower bound. The easy-target circuit has O(N^2) gates, but no small size is asserted for the actual-target baseline.

P11-P13 for the powered-slice family: restrict the available formal U circuit to a fixed base vertex using its root variable, obtaining U^(v) with no extra arithmetic gates. P=A+U^(v) is coefficientwise <=A+U=Project(Q_d) and has exact original-Delta expected coefficient loss 4/L=1/2097152<7/120. It is also the projection of the rescaled consistent branch t^d*U^(v)*(y_v/t)^d. Final coefficient domination holds although this branch violates the unscaled childwise bounds. The construction uses an explicitly available consistent factor; it does not supply one for a general gate or bound the size of the actual-target baseline A.

Candidate general-DAG construction: choose at most K interface assignments at each productive original gate. A compatible child-state join should construct a formal full-group P_D<=Project(Q) in at most 2*(g+2)*(s+1)*K^2 gates, independently of formal degree. On a one-hot input nu its coefficient should equal the value of the original shared DAG with gate v masked to zero when nu restricted to I_v is absent from its chosen dictionary. Prove these claims without assuming available semantic compatible factors.

Unproved sufficient condition for the six-fifths repair: every size-s factor-6/5 approximator of R_n admits dictionaries of at most K<=C*M_n^a*(s+1)^b states per original gate such that masking the actual shared DAG outside these dictionaries loses at most 7/120 expected output value on the original Delta. State selection and this joint loss bound must be proved; no polynomial interface width, independent group law, separate component maxima, or availability of C_v is assumed.

S10-S13: for sparse dictionaries on an arbitrary original shared DAG, reverse-topological zero-one gate cuts give the exact original-Delta loss L(D)=sum_j E_Delta[(1-z_vj)*Q_vj*H_j]. H_j is the nonnegative mixed divided-difference context with earlier masks already installed; no descendant of v_j is masked yet, so Q_vj is its original polynomial value. Pointwise 0<=Q_vj*H_j<=Q(nu), and all contexts evaluate in at most 10*(2*s+1)^2 arithmetic operations independently of formal degree. The state measure mu_j(alpha)=E_Delta[1_(nu|I_vj=alpha)*Q_vj*H_j] depends only on earlier dictionary choices; the missing joint loss is its exact sequence of discarded tails. This identity supplies no polynomial tail-concentration or efficient expectation theorem.

Diagnostic extension, not assumed for the actual target: a polynomial-size Boolean approximator of any easy full-group nonnegative target, with uniform relative defect tending to zero, admits polynomially many fixed original-interface states per gate with original-Delta expected coefficient loss <=7/120. This would justify S14 from defect and circuit size alone, without using the special arborescence coefficient pattern. Test this extension separately from C3395-BOOLEAN-WEIGHTED-PROFILE-COVER.

R1-R9: a full-original-interface carrier whose zeroing annihilates the output bounds the retained mass of any simultaneous S2 dictionaries by the weighted mass of its stored complete assignments. With only this gate restricted, the optimum is exactly the K largest weights. Under the original Delta, every atom is at most binom(L,4)^(-q). For the M_n+2-gate easy-target approximator Q_epsilon=F+(epsilon/F(1))*F^2, 0<epsilon<=1/5, the relative Boolean defect is epsilon*(F(1)-1)/(F(1)+epsilon)<epsilon, yet loss <=7/120 requires K>=(113/120)*binom(L,4)^q. Its exact projected output has only M_n gates. Conditional padding Q+(eta/F(1))*QF of an arbitrary actual factor-kappa approximator with kappa<6/5 creates the same carrier and requires K>=(31/96)*binom(L,4)^q at factor 6/5. This does not construct a small actual-target approximator, refute S14 for R_n, or lower-bound general repairs.

R10 and its preceding argument: conditional on the already supported sampler, S3-S4 constructor and N1-N4 formal lower bound, S14 as a nonuniform polynomial-dictionary existence statement is equivalent to an exponential-in-M_n unrestricted factor-6/5 lower bound for the actual R_n. S14 implies that bound by the size 2*(g+2)*(s+1)*K^2 retained circuit. Conversely, if s>=2^(c*M_n), full dictionaries have K<=product_i |X_i|<=2^M_n<=s^(1/c) and zero loss; a fixed constant handles the finite prefix. Efficient expectation evaluation is not required. This is a logical equivalence only: neither S14 nor the lower bound is proved, and the previous exact-size-transfer B2 equivalence is acknowledged rather than claimed as new.

Open: there are explicit fixed C_star>=0, K,c,e>0 and d>=0 such that every size-s nonnegative real arithmetic DAG Q, with every output monomial meeting every group and Q<=3F_G on the entire Boolean cube, satisfies Lambda_Delta(Project(Q))>=-C_star*b_Q-K*M_n^d*(s+1)^e*exp(-c*N), where b_Q=max_(F_G(X)>0)(Booleanize(Q)-Project(Q))(X)/F_G(X). Delta is the original full matching/order/embedding/bit sampler. All constants are independent of n,s,formal degree and sharing. No fixed-original-profile dictionary or gatewise sum of separate defect maxima is permitted.

For q>=1, in the original full sampler, condition only on x!=0 and choose i uniformly from {j:x_j=1}; leave the matching, order, ordered embedding and x unchanged and flip y_i. The resulting marked-history involution preserves the conditional history law, reverses the arborescence sign, changes exactly two outgoing source groups, and gives F_G(X_nu OR X_nu_prime)=4. The x=0 stratum has probability 2^(-q). On every switched union, the sum of the four independent group-corner values of a full-group Q is Project(Q) at that union, and the original shared-DAG A4 sum of mixed-context first conflicts is exactly the remainder. These identities alone do not prove signed stability.

Conditional implication only: if C3395-BOOLEAN-LOCAL-SIGNED-STABILITY holds with an explicit finite C_star, replace C_star by an explicit rational upper bound if necessary and set kappa_0=1+1/(64*(C_star+1)). Every factor-kappa_0 full-Boolean-cube approximator has Q<=3F_G, b_Q<=2*(kappa_0-kappa_0^(-1)) and C_star*b_Q<=1/16. For gamma<=1/16 its projected coefficient functional is <=-1/4, so the proposed estimate forces K*M_n^d*(s+1)^e*exp(-c*N)>=3/16 and s=2^Omega(M_n). This supplies neither the stability estimate nor an achieved approximation factor, and does not prove the separate factor-6/5 or factor-4/3 claims.

For the ordered actual DAG mixed endpoint contexts T_lambda of L10-L11 on an original local switch A=X_nu, B=X_nu_prime, let V=sum_lambda T_lambda*abs(A_lambda-B_lambda). There is an exact nonnegative decomposition V=Q(A)+Q(B)+2*Z_C+2*Z_D: Z_C is the weighted compatible mixed-corner parse mass whose B-only leaves all precede its A-only leaves, and Z_D is the corresponding incompatible mass. One has Z_C<=Q(X_01)+Q(X_10), Z_D<=D(A OR B), and each incompatible signed input flow cancels identically. A fixed upper-triangular matrix/support algebra, using at most 64 coordinates per original gate, computes both parts and gives an exact mixed-context first-conflict sum for Z_D on the shared DAG, without expanding words or counting degree. Thus E_star(2*Z_D)<=8*b_Q jointly, with no factor of s or degree. This does not control the compatible signed functional in L12 or prove L0.

Candidate unsigned shortcut to L12: there exist fixed C>=0, K,c,e>0, d>=0 such that every size-s ordered nonnegative arithmetic DAG Q with full-group-covered output and Q<=3F_G on the Boolean cube satisfies E_star V_C<=C*b_Q+K*M_n^d*(s+1)^e*exp(-c*N), where V_C is the total absolute compatible input flux of its actual L10-L11 mixed finite differences under the original full marked-history law. The candidate must hold independently of degree, sharing, and product-child order.

Open: for the actual reverse-topological compulsory-cut products Q=sum_j A_j V_j of any size-s nonnegative real arithmetic DAG with full-group-covered output and Q<=3F_G on the entire Boolean cube, put S_j=G(A_j), let k_j be the number of honored gadgets of S_j under the original embedding, and condition on the unhonored bits to form M_j on the remaining x/y bits. With good_j={k_j>=2*kappa_sampler*N/L^5} and tau_j=||M_j||_*/2^k_j, there are fixed explicit C_star>=0, K,c,e>0 and d>=0 such that sum_j E[1_good_j*2^(-k_j/2)*tau_j]<=C_star*b_Q+K*M_n^d*(s+1)^e*exp(-c*N). The expectation uses the complete original sampler, not a fixed embedding; b_Q is the one whole-output defect maximum. No size, degree, or separately optimized support-component factor may multiply b_Q.

Conditional implication only: the original-sampler spectral budget C3395-BOOLEAN-MULTIBLOCK-SPECTRAL-BUDGET implies L0 with the same C_star. For each actual cut product the conditional signed correlation is at most 2^(-k_j/2)*||M_j||_*/2^k_j in absolute value. The total bad-embedding contribution is at most 3*s*(exp(-kappa_sampler*N/4)+exp(-kappa_sampler*N/(2*L^5))). Thus replace c by min(c,kappa_sampler/(2*L^5)), e by max(e,1), and K by K+6. Reviewed L15-L16 then gives kappa_0=1+1/(64*(C_star+1)) from a proved explicit finite C_star. This establishes no spectral budget and no achieved approximation factor.

If b_Q=0 for a full-group nonnegative arithmetic DAG Q<=3F_G on the Boolean cube, each nonzero actual compulsory-cut product A_j V_j has a rank-one global coefficient array across S_j=G(A_j) and its complement. Whenever a group appears in both factors, consistency forces one common variable; the compulsory factor pins that variable and its occurrences in the other factor can be set to one on one-hot inputs. Consequently the original good-history spectral budget is at most 3*s*2^(-kappa_sampler*N/L^5), and |Lambda_Delta(Project(Q))|<=3*s*gamma. This improves the previously used zero-defect prefactor 3*((2g+1)*s+g), but supplies no uniform estimate for nonzero defects.

For every sufficiently large admissible n and fixed original q-gadget embedding E, there is an O(M_n+q^2*log(q))-size nonnegative circuit Q_E<=3F_G on the full Boolean cube, with all groups covered and b_Q<=2*(4/5)^floor(log2(q)), whose actual reverse-topological compulsory cut contains 4^floor(log2(q)) same-partition products with all q gadgets honored at E and conditional summed normalized nuclear norm at least sqrt(2). The explicit color polynomials use four-state F_4 inner-product recurrences; the actual cut, not separately selected support pieces, gives the terms. This refutes only a pointwise-in-embedding version of the spectral budget. Under the complete original sampler, the entire color-branch spectral contribution is instead at most 2*q*binom(L,4)^(-q), and the independent F_G term has the usual exponentially small good-event bound. The original averaged spectral claim, signed stability, target lower bound, novelty, and publication significance remain unresolved.

For the actual compulsory cut Q=sum_j A_j V_j, split each factor monomial by the set of optional nonroot source groups outside its compulsory side, preserving all coefficients. Let H_j be the coupled sum with total such set size at most h=floor(2^(-150)*N), and T_h=sum_(i=0)^h binom(g,i)*2^i. For every original embedding and fixing of unhonored bits, rank(M_j(H_j))<=T_h: a fixed support pair has rank at most 2^(r_x+r_y), where r_x counts honored x bits seen by V and r_y honored y bits seen by A. Under the original full sampler and good_j={k_j>=N/2^134}, the joint low-band nuclear budget is at most 3*sqrt(s*T_h)*2^(-N/2^135)<=3*sqrt(s)*exp(-N/2^137), for arbitrary nonzero defects, nonnegative real constants, sharing and degree, provided Q<=3F on the entire Boolean cube. The proof uses the common inequality sum_j H_j(X_nu)^2<=Q(X_nu)^2<=9, not separately optimized support masses. Consequently the original M3 budget differs from that of the actual coupled heavy residual by at most this remainder. This is a low-band theorem and reduction, not a proof of the remaining heavy budget or fixed-factor lower bound.

Open: for the original actual compulsory-cut products of every unrestricted size-s full-group Q<=3F_G on the Boolean cube, define W_j as the coupled sum of factor-monomial pairs whose optional nonroot source groups outside their compulsory sides have total size greater than floor(2^(-150)*N). With the same original partition S_j, full sampler, honored set, unhonored bits, and good_j as M3, prove sum_j E[1_good_j*||M_j(W_j)||_*/2^(3*k_j/2)]<=C_star*b_Q+K*M_n^d*(s+1)^e*exp(-c*N), for explicit fixed constants independent of n,s,degree and sharing, with no size or degree factor multiplying the whole-output b_Q. The W_j are semantic coupled parts of the actual products, not new products or asserted small circuits. The low-band theorem reduces M3 to this condition but does not prove it.

For each actual compulsory-cut pair H_j=A_j V_j and one common Boolean box U with F(U)>0, define the rank-one upper completion R_j,U(nu)=A_j(X_(nu_Sj) OR U_(complement Sj))*V_j(U_Sj OR X_(nu_complement Sj)). It dominates H_j(X_nu) at every corner and sum_corners(R_j,U-H_j)<=D_j(U); hence summing all actual cuts gives at most D_Q(U). Under the full original sampler, take U to be the union of all bit completions of the original pre-bit history, so F(U)=2^(4q). Conditional honored matrices inherit rank-one upper completions; disjoint unhonored-bit fibers and joint coefficient accounting give B(Q)<=3*sqrt(s)*2^(-N/2^135)+2^(1+5q/2)*b_Q. Reusing the reviewed joint bad-history bound gives |Lambda_Delta(Project(Q))|<=8*sqrt(s)*exp(-N/2^137)+2^(1+5q/2)*b_Q. This holds for arbitrary degree, sharing, repeated variables and nonnegative constants, but the exponential defect coefficient does not prove fixed-constant M3 or J10.

For the existing graph family, N=n-3>=2^142 and q=floor(N/2^23), every unrestricted nonnegative real arithmetic circuit approximating R_n=2F_G-T_G on the entire Boolean cube within symmetric factor kappa_N=1+2^(-3q-10) has size at least exp(N/2^137). The proof uses the common-box estimate, b_Q<=4*(kappa_N-1), the reviewed exact coefficient imbalance, and the original-DAG size. This is an unconditional exponentially accurate Boolean-approximation lower bound: kappa_N tends to one, so it does not prove any fixed factor greater than one or complete the current mission. No verified-new or publishable qualification is asserted.

Candidate sufficient shortcut to M3: for the common-box completions of C3395-BOOLEAN-BOX-COMPLETION, the summed good-history entrywise error mass E_1(Q)=sum_j E[1_good_j*||R_j,z-M_j,z||_1/2^(3*k_j/2)] is at most C*b_Q+K*M_n^d*(s+1)^e*exp(-c*N), with fixed C>=0, K,c,e>0, d>=0 independent of degree and sharing. The box is U_eta, the union of all bit completions of the original pre-bit history; the sum is only over actual cut products, with the original sampler and full-cube Q<=3F. This is stronger than a nuclear-error estimate and is not J10 itself.

Open: for the exact J2-J3 coupled heavy matrices M_j=M_j(W_j) of every full-group unrestricted nonnegative real arithmetic DAG Q<=3F_G on the entire Boolean cube, define m_j=2^k_j, a_j=sum(M_j)/m_j^2, beta_j=||M_j||_*/m_j^(3/2), and beta_j^2/a_j=0 if a_j=0. Under the unchanged full original sampler and good events, there are explicit fixed C>=0, K,c,e>0 and d>=0 such that E_heavy=sum_j E[1_good_j*beta_j^2/a_j]<=C*b_Q+K*M_n^d*(s+1)^e*exp(-c*N). The sum is only over actual cut products, coefficients and semantic heavy components are unchanged, and no size or degree factor multiplies b_Q. This is a sufficient square-root route, not the stronger linear J10 and not a proved estimate.

Conditional reduction: the exact J2-J3 matrices satisfy sum_j E[1_good_j*a_j]<=3 and B_heavy^2<=3*E_heavy under one common original law. Their energy is the infimum of (tr(P_j)+tr(R_j))^2/(4*m_j^3*a_j) over PSD blocks [P_j M_j; M_j^T R_j], with zero convention when a_j=0. If C3395-BOOLEAN-HEAVY-ENERGY holds with an explicit rational upper bound C, then J12 implies an unrestricted fixed-factor lower bound at kappa_0=1+1/(768*(C+1)): sqrt(3*C*b_Q)<1/8 and the exact coefficient imbalance exceeds 7/16, leaving a gap greater than 5/16 for a polynomial-in-size exponentially decaying remainder. The same comparison covers factor 6/5 only for energy coefficient C<49/1980, and factor 4/3 only for C<1/504. No finite C, energy estimate, or fixed-factor lower bound is asserted.

Conditional reduction: the exact J2-J3 matrices satisfy sum_j E[1_good_j*a_j]<=3 and B_heavy^2<=3*E_heavy under one common original law. Their energy is the infimum of (tr(P_j)+tr(R_j))^2/(4*m_j^3*a_j) over PSD blocks [P_j M_j; M_j^T R_j], with zero convention when a_j=0. If C3395-BOOLEAN-HEAVY-ENERGY holds with an explicit rational upper bound C, then J12 implies an unrestricted fixed-factor lower bound at kappa_0=1+1/(768*(C+1)): sqrt(3*C*b_Q)<1/8 and the exact coefficient imbalance exceeds 7/16, leaving a gap greater than 5/16 for a polynomial-in-size exponentially decaying remainder. The same comparison covers factor 6/5 only for energy coefficient C<49/1980, and factor 4/3 only for C<1/504. No finite C, energy estimate, or fixed-factor lower bound is asserted.

claims.natural_statement: For the exact J2-J3 coupled heavy matrices of an unrestricted full-group Q<=3F_G on the Boolean cube, b_Q=0 implies E_heavy<=3*s*(D_h+1)*2^(-k0)<=6*s*exp(-N/2^136). The reviewed zero-defect full-product matrices have rank at most one, the low matrices have rank at most D_h, and the heavy matrices therefore have rank at most D_h+1. Since heavy entries are in [0,3], their nuclear energy beta_j^2/a_j is at most 3*(D_h+1)/m_j, also with the zero-mass convention. This is an all-size exactly-zero-defect theorem, not a modulus at positive defect or a fixed-factor lower bound.

For T=J_3-I_3 and every ell>=1, ||T^(tensor ell)||_*=4^ell, whereas the infimum of sum_l ||u_l||_2*||v_l||_2 over nonnegative-coordinate factorizations T^(tensor ell)=sum_l u_l v_l^T is (3*sqrt(2))^ell. Every supported atom rectangle has area at most 2^ell and total matrix mass is 6^ell; row atoms attain the bound. The exact PSD block with P=I_3+J_3/3 and off-diagonal T has half trace 4, dual witness Z=2*J_3/3-I_3, and characteristic polynomial z^3*(z-4)*(z-2)^2, despite admitting no nonnegative-coordinate Gram factor at that cost. Padding T by a zero row and column realizes the gap in the entire heavy part of one actual cut of the O(M_n+q)-gate full-cube circuit Q=F+lambda*m_E*(P_ell^2+D_A*P_ell), q=2*ell, 0<lambda<=1. At its fixed embedding the true energy is 2*lambda*(2/3)^ell, the restricted cost is 2*lambda*(3/4)^ell, and b_Q<=2*lambda. Under the original sampler its actual heavy energy is at most 2*lambda*binom(L,4)^(-q). Thus only a dimension-independent comparison between positive-coordinate Gram cost and nuclear cost is excluded; the original-sampler energy estimate, a direct bound on positive-coordinate costs, J10 and the target lower bound are not refuted. No novelty is asserted.

For the exact J2-J3 coupled heavy matrices of every unrestricted full-group Q<=3F_G on the Boolean cube, beta_j^2<=3*a_j. Consequently, for every t>0, the good-history nuclear sum restricted to a_j<t is at most sqrt(3)*s*sqrt(t), under the unchanged original law and with original circuit size. At t_N=2^(-N/2^134), this thin sum is at most 2*s*exp(-N/2^136), for arbitrary positive defect. Defining E_thick=sum_j E[1_good_j*1_(a_j>=t_N)*beta_j^2/a_j], the reviewed common-law budget and J12 give |Lambda_Delta(Project(Q))|<=sqrt(3*E_thick)+10*(s+1)*exp(-N/2^137). Therefore a fixed-coefficient bound E_thick<=C*b_Q+K*M_n^d*(s+1)^e*exp(-c*N), if proved, would give the reviewed explicit factor 1+1/(768*(C+1)) with remainder constants sqrt(3*K)+10, d/2, max(e/2,1) and min(c/2,2^(-137)). This proves only removal of the small-mean nuclear sector and a conditional transfer; neither the thick estimate, full E4, nor a fixed-factor lower bound is asserted.

For k=9^t, q=2*k^2*4^k and admissible N=2^23*q, let D=2*sqrt(k) and epsilon=2^(-D). The F_4 Fourier graph code on (Z/3)^(2t) has 2*k message bits, bijective halves and binary distance at least D; tensor it in q/(2*k) chunks. For every fixed original q-gadget embedding E, its code polynomial P has a shared O(q*4^k)-gate circuit. The full-group Q=m_E*(P^2+epsilon*D_A*P) has original size O(M_n+q^2), full-cube Q<3F_G, and epsilon/4<=b_Q<=2*epsilon tending to zero. Building V=m_B*P before A=m_S*(P+epsilon*D_A) makes AV the sole nonzero actual cut; the entire cut is heavy because V uses 2q optional nonroot sources. At E its matrix is (1+epsilon) times a permutation matrix of order 2^q, so a=(1+epsilon)/2^q, beta=(1+epsilon)/2^(q/2), and actual nuclear energy beta^2/a=1+epsilon. Thus even a one-cut historywise E4-type bound with whole-output defect and polynomial-in-original-size exponentially decaying remainder fails. The actual averaged energy is instead at most (1+epsilon)*binom(L,4)^(-q), since the branch vanishes off its fixed active source set. This is not a counterexample to E4 under the original sampler, not a small R_n approximator and not a lower bound. Unlike the prior many-color obstruction, only one actual cut is used; unlike the positive-coordinate gap, the actual nuclear energy is large. No novelty or publication qualification is claimed.

Open weaker sufficient condition, not a proof of full E4: for the exact J2-J3 coupled heavy matrices of every unrestricted full-group Q<=3F_G, with the original sampler, original good events and t_N=2^(-N/2^134), there are explicit fixed C>=0, K,c,e>0 and d>=0 such that sum_j E[1_good_j*1_(a_j>=t_N)*beta_j^2/a_j]<=C*b_Q+K*M_n^d*(s+1)^e*exp(-c*N). Sum only actual cut products, preserve all coefficients, nonnegative real constants, sharing, repeated variables and unbounded formal degree, and permit no size or degree multiplier on b_Q. The small-conditional-mean nuclear sector is already exponentially small with polynomial original-size cost. This thick-sector energy estimate remains unproved and is an alternative sufficient route to the same fixed-factor objective, not a relaxation of that objective.

For all admissible N>=2^142, original shared-DAG size s, full-group Q<=3F_G on the Boolean cube, and precisely the J2-J3 coupled heavy matrices, the original-sampler thick energy on k_j>=k0=N/2^134 and a_j>=2^(-k0) is at most 9*2^(2q+k0)*b_Q+2^16*s*exp(-5*k0/32), q=floor(N/2^23). This is an unconditional positive-defect estimate with no size or degree multiplier on b_Q, but its exponential dimension coefficient does not establish T5. A self-contained Haar expansion bounds the nuclear norm of any m=2^k square matrix in [0,B] whose rows are nondecreasing in a common column order by B*m*(1+k/2). Apply it to the bounded clipping of each original rank-one upper completion, without claiming clipped rank one or positive-coordinate Gram optimality. The exact heavy identity is W=min(R,3)-(min(R,3)-M_full)-M_low. Clipped error is in [0,3] and dominated by the original completion error, enabling a Frobenius estimate. The original common-box defect is summed over actual cuts before averaging or taking b_Q. An original-sampler tail bounds k_j<5*k0/4 by exp(-N/2^22)+exp(-5*k0/32). All coefficients, arbitrary nonnegative real constants, sharing, repeated variables, unrestricted degree and original-size cost are retained; no efficient semantic extraction is asserted. No fixed-factor lower bound or novelty qualification is claimed.

For every admissible N>=2^146, q=floor(N/2^23), k0=N/2^134 and kappa_N=1+2^(-(2q+ceil(k0)+14)), every unrestricted nonnegative real arithmetic circuit approximating the existing R_n=2F_G-T_G within symmetric factor kappa_N on the entire Boolean cube has original size s>=exp(N/2^137). The clipped thick-energy bound and the reviewed common-law square-root transfer give defect contribution at most sqrt(27)/64<1/8; retaining separately the thin and low/bad remainders gives less than 1/16 more if s<exp(k0/8) and k0>=4096, contradicting the reviewed exact coefficient gap greater than 7/16. Compared with K6 alone, which already permits the sharper preceding window 2^(-(ceil(5q/2)+10)) rather than just displayed K8, the new allowed error is larger by 2^(ceil(q/2)-ceil(k0)-4). Thus the same exponential size exponent holds in a strictly broader shrinking-accuracy regime, with the larger stated N cutoff. The factor still tends to one exponentially. This is not T5, E4 or any fixed-factor lower bound, and neither verified novelty nor publication qualification is asserted.

For the exact original cut and original K1 common-box completions, set Eprime_j=min(R_j,3)-M_j(Q_j), a_j=mean(M_j(W_j)), m_j=2^k_j and k0=N/2^134. Define Nerr=sum_j E[1_(k_j>=5*k0/4)*1_(a_j>=2^(-k0))*||Eprime_j||_*^2/(m_j^3*a_j)] under the unchanged original sampler and unhonored-bit fixing. For every admissible N>=2^142 and full-group unrestricted Q<=3F_G, E_thick<=3*Nerr+2^16*s*exp(-5*k0/32) and Nerr<=3*E_thick+2^16*s*exp(-5*k0/32). This follows from both directions of W=min(R,3)-Eprime-M_low and the reviewed V2,V8,V10 bounds, without entrywise substitution. Consequently a dimension-independent whole-output defect bound for Nerr is equivalent to T5 with constants 3C, 3K+2^16, alpha, max(beta,1), min(c,5/2^139). This is an equivalence, not proof of either defect bound. The original size, coefficients, unrestricted degree, constants, sharing and common law are unchanged; stronger linear J10 is unnecessary.

Open nuclear-error charge Z3, equivalent up to fixed constants to T5: under the original sampler, sum only actual cuts of 1_(k_j>=5*k0/4)*1_(a_j>=2^(-k0))*||min(R_j,3)-M_j(Q_j)||_*^2/(m_j^3*a_j) in expectation and bound the result by C*b_Q+K*M_n^alpha*(s+1)^beta*exp(-c*N), with explicit fixed C>=0, K,c,beta>0 and alpha>=0. Here R_j is exactly the original common-box rank-one upper completion, a_j is the conditional mean of the exact J2-J3 heavy matrix, and m_j=2^k_j. Preserve all coefficients, full-cube Q<=3F, arbitrary nonnegative real constants, sharing, repeated variables, unrestricted degree and original-DAG cost. The bounded relative entrywise-mass proxy is refuted separately; its counterexample has exponentially small true nuclear error and does not refute this charge.

Proposed universal shortcut Z5, submitted for refutation: for the original common-box completions Eprime_j=min(R_j,3)-M_j(Q_j), the actual J2-J3 heavy conditional means a_j and m_j=2^k_j, there are fixed C>=0, K,c,beta>0 and alpha>=0 with sum_j E[1_(k_j>=5*k0/4)*1_(a_j>=2^(-k0))*sum(Eprime_j)/(m_j^2*a_j)]<=C*b_Q+K*M_n^alpha*(s+1)^beta*exp(-c*N) for every unrestricted full-group Q<=3F_G. The law is the full original sampler. This is the bounded relative entrywise relaxation of the nuclear-error energy, not T5 itself, not unbounded K11, and not a historywise estimate.

For every admissible N>=2^154 there is an O(M_n+N^2)-gate nonnegative rational circuit with one actual cut that is entirely J2 heavy, full-cube Q<=zeta*F_G and b_Q<=zeta=2^(-ceil(k0/4)) tending to zero. A fixed packing of v=floor(N/512) base edges with disjoint edge-mark neighborhoods gives distinguished nonroot variables Y, with all endpoints in a fixed balanced side B. Put d=floor(N/2^150)+1, r=floor(N/2^67), lambda=binom(r,d)/binom(v,d), a_star=zeta*lambda, U_k the full-B polynomial selecting exactly k variables of Y, V=sum_(k>=r) U_k/binom(k,d), and A=a_star*F_S*e_d(Y). Build V before A, so AV is the sole actual cut and every A monomial has exactly d optional nonroot sources. Projection is a_star*F_S*sum_(k>=r)U_k. Under the original random matching/order/tuple/bit law, selected Y count K and available-but-unselected count ell-K are both at least N/2^66 except probability exp(-N/2^19)+2*exp(-N/2^68). Since a_star>=2^(-k0/2), the thick event and k>=5*k0/4 hold with probability tending to one. The capped relative error statistic of Z5 is at least (exp(N/2^208)-1)/2, although Eprime=R-M<=zeta so clipping at three is inactive. Thus no fixed coefficients in Z5 exist. In contrast all actual heavy and error matrices have identical rows: E_thick<=a_star*2^(-k0) and true nuclear-error budget Nerr<=2^(-3*k0/4). This refutes only the capped relative-mass shortcut, not T5, E4, the nuclear-error charge, adaptive amplitude bounds or the target lower bound. Unlike K11 the entire cut is heavy and its conditional mean is thick; unlike fixed-history constructions the obstruction survives the full sampler. No verified novelty or publication qualification is claimed.

For the unchanged Z1 capped errors Eprime_j, heavy means a_j, dimensions m_j=2^k_j and indicators I_j=1_(k_j>=5*k0/4)*1_(a_j>=2^(-k0)), put P_j=11^T/m_j and X_j=(I-P_j)Eprime_j(I-P_j). Then Ncenter=sum_j E[I_j*||X_j||_*^2/(m_j^3*a_j)] satisfies Ncenter<=Nerr<=2*Ncenter+36*s*2^(-k0/4). Moreover Ncenter is exactly the supremum, over all conditionally measurable real matrices Y_j with P_j Y_j=Y_j P_j=0, of sum_j E[I_j*(2*<Y_j,X_j>/m_j^(3/2)-a_j*||Y_j||op^2)]. This finite-dimensional bridge is not a defect charge or a fixed-factor theorem.

Under the original pre-bit law, take uniform b in {0,1}^(2q) and independent flips e with probability p=1/(2q) per bit. The common Boolean union Ustar=X_b OR X_(b xor e) has F(Ustar)=4^|e| and normalization Z=(1+3/(2q))^(2q)<=exp(3). Every cut-specific mixed corner obtained by flipping only its honored row and/or column bits retains the original marginal and lies below Ustar. Weighting by F(Ustar)/Z preserves these marginals and replaces p by 4p/(1+3p). A4/A7 therefore give a single joint unnormalized defect budget E[D_Q(Ustar)]<=Z*b_Q, with no cut-count multiplier. For k>=5*k0/4, projecting Eprime onto Walsh degrees at least floor(k/256) on both sides loses at most 36*s*2^(-11*k0/64) in the two-sided nuclear-energy reduction, while the inverse of I-T_p on those degrees has operator norm at most 2^121. Sparse-noise polarization is an exact signed identity, not a proof that its pairing is bounded by the joint defect budget.

Open: there are explicit fixed C>=0, K,c,beta>0 and alpha>=0 such that, for every allowed unrestricted full-group Q<=3F and every conditionally measurable centered real matrix family Y_j, sum_j E[I_j*(2*<Y_j,(I-P_j)Eprime_j(I-P_j)>/m_j^(3/2)-a_j*||Y_j||op^2)]<=C*b_Q+K*M_n^alpha*(s+1)^beta*exp(-c*N), with exactly the original Z1 errors, heavy conditional means, strong-good/thick indicators and full original sampler. The supremum is the centered nuclear energy. The centering bridge and Z2 would transfer its coefficient to T5 as 6C. No such charge is established by a variational identity, a common sparse-noise defect budget, or a conditional diagnostic.

Candidate remainder-free pointwise shortcut, distinct from the averaged charge: there exists a finite C such that every allowed full-group Q<=3F, every supported original history with the sparse p=1/(2q) two-copy coupling, and every conditionally measurable high-frequency family Y_j=H_j Y_j H_j satisfy sum_j I_j*((sqrt(m_j)/2)*delta(B_j Y_j B_j)*delta(Eprime_j)-a_j*||Y_j||op^2)<=C*D_Q(Ustar) pointwise. Here H_j projects to Walsh degrees at least floor(k_j/256), B_j is its inverse of I-T_p, and the original heavy means and Z1 errors are unchanged. No additive remainder is allowed in this shortcut. If true, CD7 and CD10-CD12 would yield a dimension-independent averaged charge.

CD18-CD20: for every sufficiently large admissible N, a fixed supported original pre-bit history and a balanced side containing all its row sources give an O(M_n+q+d)-gate allowed circuit with one actual cut Q=A*V<=3F, d=floor(N/2^150)+1. Positive parity recurrences give f_S=F_S+P_even,S and V=F_B+P_even,B, where the column parity avoids d distinguished optional nonroot source groups; set A=(f_S/2)*(1+C_D/2). Its optional branch is exactly heavy. At the specified history all k=q gadgets are honored, its heavy mean is a=(9/16)*2^(-d)>=2^(-k0), and Xhi=chi_U*chi_W*(1-c)/16 has squared operator norm m^2*(1-2^(-d))/256. Flipping one row bit and one column bit outside the optional set while leaving all optional variables absent gives D_Q(Ustar)=0, but the CD12 regularized signed integrand for the conditionally fixed Y=m^(-2)*Xhi is at least 247/(8192*m^2)>0. Thus the remainder-free pointwise shortcut fails for every finite C with the actual heavy threshold. This does not refute the averaged charge: at every original history the error is bounded by one and has rank at most one, so this family has Nerr<=2^(-k0/4).

For the actual cut Q_j=A_j V_j, use the four actual one-hot corners from CD5 and their local union U_j, not the global completion error. For their nonnegative two-square value matrix Z_j, define phi(Z)=det(Z)^2/(sum Z)^3 and phi(0)=0. The K1 local rank-one upper completion gives phi(Z_j)<=D_Qj(U_j), including repeated corners. Consequently the unchanged CD5 sparse coupling and A4/A7 give sum_j E_mu phi(Z_j)<=exp(3)*b_Q, with one whole-output defect budget and no size multiplier. This local inequality is not a nuclear-tail charge.

For admissible N>=2^142, let M_j=M_j(Q_j), L_j=M_j(H_j), W_j=M_j(W_j), a_j=mean(W_j), m_j=2^k_j, I_j=1_(k_j>=5*k0/4,a_j>=2^(-k0)), and r_j=floor(2^(k_j/8)), retaining the original sampler and actual cut. If tau_j is the sum of singular values of M_j after its largest r_j values and T=sum_j E[I_j*tau_j^2/(m_j^3*a_j)], then T<=E_thick<=3*T+54*s*2^(-3*k0/32)+6*s*exp(-5*k0/32). Thus a fixed-coefficient defect bound for T is equivalent up to fixed constants to T5. Its coefficient C would give T5 coefficient 3C and the reviewed factor 1+1/(768*(3C+1)); no such coefficient is established. Rank truncation is an analysis operation, not an asserted efficient circuit extraction.

Open: for the exact actual-cut matrices, original heavy means and indicators in C3395-BOOLEAN-RANK-TAIL-REDUCTION, prove T(Q)<=C*b_Q+K*M_n^alpha*(s+1)^beta*exp(-c*N) with explicit fixed C>=0, K,c,beta>0 and alpha>=0. Preserve all coefficients, arbitrary nonnegative real constants, sharing, repeated variables, unrestricted degree, full-cube Q<=3F and original-DAG size. No entrywise proxy, embeddingwise estimate or automatic conversion from a local minor budget is assumed. The local minor budget and SVD equivalence do not prove this charge or the fixed-factor lower bound.

Open sufficient circuit-specific gluing condition: T(Q)<=C0*sum_j E_mu phi(Z_j)+K*M_n^alpha*(s+1)^beta*exp(-c*N), with explicit size-independent constants and precisely the actual cuts, original heavy means, sparse coupling, original full outer sampler and original-DAG size of RG1-RG4. The local minor budget would give C3395-BOOLEAN-RANK-TAIL-CHARGE with coefficient exp(3)*C0. This is not a matrix-only assertion and is not proved or refuted by a designated-history matrix example. A direct whole-output defect bound for T remains an alternative.

Candidate generic sufficient shortcut, not the mission: there are fixed C,K,c>0 and d>=0 such that for every k0>=256, integer k>=5*k0/4, q>=k, m=2^k, r=floor(m^(1/8)), and nonnegative matrices 0<=L<=M<=3 with rank(L)<=r and a=mean(M-L)>=2^(-k0), the singular-value tail of M satisfies tau_r(M)^2/(m^3*a)<=C*E phi(Z)+K*k^d*exp(-c*k0). Here Z consists of the four actual entries of M under uniform row and column bits and independent flips of probability 1/(2q), and phi(0)=0. No circuit realization or original outer averaging is imposed in this stronger matrix-only claim.

RG9-RG12 refutes only the matrix-only shortcut. For t=4^ell, m=t^2=2^k, k=4*ell and k0=3*ell, let B_(x,y),(a,b)=1_(y=a*x+b) over F_t, M=J/2+B and L=J/2. Then the actual heavy mean a=mean(B)=1/t meets the strong-good/thick conditions, rank(L)=1, and all full entries are between 1/2 and 3/2. The complete singular spectrum of M is (m/2+t)^1, sqrt(t)^(t*(t-1)), and 0^(t-1). For r=floor(t^(1/4)), tau_r(M)^2/(m^3*a)=(1-1/t-(r-1)/t^2)^2 tends to one, whereas every four-corner coupling with uniform corner marginals has E phi(Z)<=1/(8*t). Thus no fixed minor-energy multiple plus a polynomial-in-k exponential remainder suffices for arbitrary matrices. A paired-group actual-cut diagnostic realizes these conditional matrices with Q<=3F/2, but its explicit size is O(k*t^3), its whole-cube defect is at least 1/2, and no full-original-sampler counterexample is supplied. The actual averaged charge, T5 and the fixed-factor target remain open.

Open: uniformly for all actual size-s unrestricted nonnegative real arithmetic DAGs satisfying R_n/kappa <= Q <= kappa*R_n on the full Boolean cube, 1<kappa<=65/64, there are explicit alpha>0, C>=0, K,c,e>0 and d>=0 independent of kappa,n,s and formal degree such that -Lambda_Delta(Project(Q_heavy)) <= C*b_Q^alpha+K*M_n^d*(s+1)^e*exp(-c*N). Q_heavy is exactly J2 for the actual compulsory cut, with all multiplicities and original sampler retained. This assertion neither assumes an unsigned heavy-mass bound nor RG8 nor deletion-only repair.

claims.natural_statement: BP4-BP9: For each fixed Boolean box X and the actual J2 cut there are at most s coefficient-preserving heavy subpolynomials P_j, each nonzero one pinned at at least floor(h/2)+1 nonroot source groups, with total residual at X at most sqrt(2*Q(X)*D_Q(X)). Under the actual approximation promise this is at most 2*sqrt(kappa*b_Q)*F(X), and relative to Q(X) at most sqrt(2*kappa*b_Q). For any such choices fixed before the original sampler, including any sampler-independent convex mixture, their joint mean is at most 2*kappa*s*(4/L)^max(floor(h/2)-1,0) <=3*s*exp(-N/2^149) for N>=2^153. The two hubs are excluded from the fixed base-source count. The local choices can depend on X; no global signed stability is asserted.

Generic sufficient strengthening being tested: fixed C>=0,alpha>0,K,d,e exist such that every size-s full-group nonnegative real circuit Q with F/2<=Q<=3F on the Boolean cube admits arbitrary nonnegative pinned polynomials B_a, each with at least floor(h/2)-1 fixed base nonroot source pins, sum_a max_nu B_a(X_nu)<=K*M_n^d*(s+1)^e, and sum_a B_a(X)>=Q_heavy(X)-C*b_Q^alpha on every one-hot input. Rewriting is permitted and coefficient domination is not required. This is stronger than the actual-target signed sampler goal.

BP10-BP16: t disjoint moving-source blocks of 2k base groups yield C=product_i C_i and P=F_rest*C. For H=F or actual R_n, Q_H=(H-P)+F_rest*(C+C^2)/2 has Project(Q_H)=H, exact b_Q=4^(-k), and H<=Q_H<=(1+4^(-k))*H on every Boolean input. For k>=3 the actual-target version satisfies kappa<=65/64. A specified original gate order has exactly heavy part F_rest*C^2/2 when kt>h. Q_F has O(M_n+kt) gates; no small circuit is asserted for the actual-target baseline R_n-P. On the uniform 2^t codewords, any arbitrary nonnegative pin family with at least ell fixed base pins and residual at most epsilon has aggregate one-hot maximum at least (1/2-epsilon)*2^ceil(ell/k). For k=ceil(log2 N), t=floor(N/(8*L*k)), ell=floor(h/2)-1, this is superpolynomial in the easy original size for epsilon=C*b_Q^alpha. In contrast its absolute original-Delta heavy mass is at most 2^(t-1)*(4/L)^(kt)<=2^(-20*kt-1). This refutes only the generic uniform-box strengthening, not the actual-target polynomial-in-original-size signed modulus or RG8.

Open: for the actual J2 heavy cut of every unrestricted size-s full-Boolean approximator R_n/kappa <= Q <= kappa*R_n, 1<kappa<=65/64, construct a finite family of nonnegative full-group polynomials P_i and base-source pin sets I_i, fixed before the original sampler, with |I_i|>=max(floor(h/2)-1,0). Put rho=4/L=2^(-21), A_i=max over all one-hot assignments of P_i, and Z=Project(Q_heavy)-sum_i P_i. Prove sum_i A_i*rho^|I_i|-Lambda_Delta(Z)<=C*b_Q^alpha+K*M_n^d*(s+1)^e*exp(-c*N) with explicit size-independent alpha,c,K,e>0 and C,d>=0. Repeated pins use set union, the hubs are excluded, all coefficients and shared contexts remain accounted for, and Z may be signed.

Candidate generic sufficient shortcut, not an accepted theorem: for every full-group original monotone DAG Q<=3F on the Boolean cube, group each directional heavy factor by its exact compatible-neighbor set in the opposite factor, with all coefficients retained. For the resulting full-group projected pieces use their maximal common base-nonroot pin sets and their global one-hot maxima. Their total rho-weighted pin budget is at most C*b_Q^alpha+K*M_n^d*(s+1)^e*exp(-c*N), with size-independent positive constants and rho=2^(-21). No actual-target lower promise is assumed in this stronger generic shortcut.

WP1-WP3: Every actual J2 heavy cut admits a finite coefficient-preserving expansion Project(Q_heavy)=sum_i P_i into sampler-independent nonnegative full-group pieces pinned at at least ell=max(floor(h/2)-1,0) fixed base sources.
